1. The present appeal is filed by the original claimant under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act,
1988 (hereinafter referred to as the "Act, 1988") being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment and award dated 24/04/2014 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Main),
Kachchh at Bhuj in MACP No.1072 of 1998.

sentences.text:
2. Short facts of the claim case are as under:
2.1. On fateful day the deceased Sumar Salemamad Changal NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2260/2014 JUDGMENT DATED: 08/08/2025 undefined was going from Bhuj to Pandhro along with truck bearing registration no.GJ-12-T-9626 for loading the lignite.
He was driving the truck while in employment of opponent no.1.
He was driving the truck in moderate and controllable speed in left side of the road.
While overtaking the truck giving the signals for overtaking, the truck turned turtle and the accident took place.
The accident took place around 21:00 hours two kilometers away from Todai Fatak on Bhuj- Nakhatrana Pandhro road.
In the accident Sumar Salemamad Changal sustained serious injuries and succumbed to the same.

2.2. The appellants-original claimants therefore filed claim petition under the provisions of Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 claiming compensation of Rs.19,00,000/- against the respondents.

2.3. Vide the aforesaid impugned judgment and award, the Tribunal has partly allowed the claim petition preferred by the appellants-original claimants under Section 166 of the Act, 1988 holding the appellants-original claimants are entitled to an amount of Rs.5,96,000/- with interest at the rate of 10% per annum from the date of filing of such claim petition till its actual realization with proportionate costs.

3. This Court vide order dated 01/08/2014, noticing the submissions made by the learned advocate for the appellants- original claimants and the grounds raised in the present appeal, has admitted the appeal.
NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2260/2014 JUDGMENT DATED: 08/08/2025 undefined

4. The learned advocate appearing on behalf of the appellants-original claimants has submitted that the Tribunal has committed an error in awarding inadequate compensation to the claimants and has failed to appreciate the evidence on record in its true perspective.

He has further submitted that the Tribunal has not properly assessed the income of the deceased and has overlooked the settled principles of law in relation to the assessment of other conventional heads also like loss of consortium, loss of estate, funeral and transportation expenses etc.

The learned advocate has therefore submitted that the compensation awarded is not just, fair, and reasonable and it is required to be enhanced in accordance with the settled legal principles.
4.1. Learned advocate has assailed the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal and submitted that the Tribunal has wrongly considered income of the deceased as Rs.3,000/- per month only without appreciating the evidence produced on record.
He has vehemently argued that the deceased was also receiving daily wages which should be included in the income of the deceased while calculating the income of the deceased.

He has submitted that the amount awarded under Salmabai Sumar Changal vs Champaklal Ravilal Karani on 8 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/5453251/
2 various conventional heads are also on the lower side.

sentences.text: By making the aforesaid submissions, learned advocate for the appellants-original claimants has urged this Court to enhance the amount of compensation accordingly which may be awarded with interest at the rate of 12% per annum from the date of filing of claim petition till its actual NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2260/2014 JUDGMENT DATED: 08/08/2025 undefined realization.

5. Learned advocate appearing for the other side has placed reliance upon the findings and reasons assigned by the Tribunal and vehemently argued that the compensation must be awarded as just,
proper and reasonable and further submitted that learned Tribunal, after appreciating the materials available on record, awarded the compensation under each head which is just, proper and reasonable and not required to be interfered in this appeal and lastly prayed to dismiss the present appeal.

6. Heard learned advocates appearing for the respective parties on the disputes between the parties in narrow compass and perused the record and proceedings and impugned judgment and award,
more particularly, the findings and reasons assigned by the Tribunal while considering the issue of quantum of compensation.
7.

As regards the submissions made by the learned advocate for the appellants-original claimants on the issue of assessment of the income is concerned, the Tribunal has not committed any error in assessing the income of the deceased and the same appears to be appropriate as it appears that the same is considered after appreciating material evidence on record and considering 45 years of age of the deceased as per the postmortem report.

Noticing the fact that the age of the deceased was considered as 45 years on the basis of the postmortem report by the learned tribunal, in light of the NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2260/2014 JUDGMENT DATED: 08/08/2025 undefined decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Sarla Verma and ors. vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and Anr. reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121 and the schedule prescribed, multiplier of 14 is appropriate.

sentences.text: Further, in view of the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd (supra), the claimants would be entitled to enhance amount of compensation under the head of loss of consortium also.

Lastly, the amount to be awarded under the conventional heads, more particularly, funeral expenses and the loss of estate is also required to be reconsidered in view of the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Pranay Sethi (supra).
8.

sentences.text: The appellant-original claimant is held entitled to total compensation of an amount of Rs.8,79,100/-.

Since by impugned judgment and award the Tribunal has awarded an amount of Rs.5,96,000/-, the appellants shall be entitled to enhanced amount of compensation to the tune of Rs.2,83,100/-
(Rs.8,79,100/- - Rs.5,96,000/-) with interest at the rate of 8% on enhanced amount of compensation from the date of filing of claim petition till its actual realization.
The respondents-original opponents are held liable to pay such enhanced amount of compensation as per the award of the tribunal.

11. Let, such exercise be undertaken by the Tribunal strictly in accordance with the guidelines prescribed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in this regard; preferably within a period of two weeks from deposit of such amount.

The Tribunal is directed to realize the deficit Court fees before proceeding with the disbursement of the amount.
12. Record and proceedings be sent back to the concerned tribunal forthwith, if received.
